title: Eval-mediated canary sequencer for catalog and tenant pin upgrades
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Implement an automated canary sequencer that runs targeted evals when a model version is pinned or upgraded (both catalog-level promotions and tenant-specific pins). The sequencer will orchestrate staged evals (smoke -> fidelity -> safety) against tenant samples and catalog testbeds, score deltas against baselines, and surface pass/fail signals to the rollout engine. Goals: (1) catch regressions early with low cost, (2) integrate with existing rollout policies so upgrades can be paused or rolled back automatically, (3) provide observability + audit trail for every pin event. This ticket covers the product design, sampling policy, gating thresholds, and acceptance criteria; engineering tickets will implement the sequencer service and hooks into the eval runner and rollout engine.
acceptance_criteria: Canary sequencer accepts pin events from catalog or tenant pin API and schedules a preflight eval plan within configured budget
Sequencer supports three staged eval types: smoke (fast correctness), fidelity (domain metrics), safety (policy checks) and runs them in order
Default tenant sampling policy is applied (1% production sampling or synthetic tenant probe depending on tenant preference) and can be overridden per-tenant

Automated gate: if fidelity delta drops by >7% relative to baseline OR safety violation rate increases by >2 percentage points, the sequencer emits a FAIL and triggers rollout pause and an automated rollback webhook
Evaluation results are recorded in the eval store and visible in the Console rollout page with per-metric deltas, confidence bounds, and links to raw examples
Audit trail written for every pin event with links to PRs, release notes, and who approved the promotion
design_notes: Use layered eval plan: quick smoke tests run first (max 30s), fidelity tests next (batch up to 500 samples), safety checks last (asynchronous but must complete before final pass)

Sampling: tenant-aware sampler picks either live traffic shadow samples (costly, high-fidelity) or tenant-supplied synthetic probes when available; default is synthetic probes + 1% live sampling for high-traffic tenants
Cost guard: per-pin budget default $75 evaluation spend; sequencer must respect tenant-level budget override to avoid runaway eval charges
Failing fast: if smoke tests fail, abort remaining stages and mark FAIL immediately to save cost
Fallback integration: call rollout engine API with statuses {PASS, WARN, FAIL} and suggestions (pause, rollback, continue-with-monitoring)
Versioning: tie eval results to pinned model SHA and config diff to make postmortems deterministic
tradeoffs: Stricter thresholds reduce customer risk but increase false positives and manual work for PMs/SEs
Heavy reliance on live sampling gives more realistic signal but increases cost and risk of exposing model mistakes in production shadowing
Large tenant-specific probes require coordination with the tenant; default to synthetic probes when coordination is infeasible
Running full fidelity suites for every small pin would be expensive; prefer staged approach and sampled fidelity runs
